sentences.text: Good morning. There are four stories today. Answers to your follow-up questions come first.
Our biggest story is about Nvidia and its chips in Southeast Asia.
Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia.
Partners named include Dell and Super Micro. The pause has no set end date.
It lasts while Nvidia checks whether regional partners meet U.S. export requirements.
Chinese companies had been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in these countries.
The U.S. Commerce Department closed that loophole earlier this month.
The Institute for Progress estimates these remote data centers supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.
Next, a story for you on a team of AI agents doing advanced math.
Anthropic researcher Lance Martin says 1,000 Claude agents self-coordinated over 30 hours to formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean without a domain-specific harness.
The run had no domain-specific harness and no human steering on the solution.
The lead agent created database tables to coordinate the team, though it was never told to.
The agents' only tools were Git and a SQL database.
Now, a story for you on small modular reactors.
The Tennessee Valley Authority became the first U.S. power utility authorized to build a commercial small modular reactor.
The project will use GE Vernova Hitachi's BWRX-300 reactor. The TVA has not set a date to break ground.
Over 120 distinct designs are recorded globally, up from 83 in 2022, but many have not been licensed.
Last, a story for you on AI that generates long videos.
Its memory agent reads only the prompts so far, never the generated video.
On a new benchmark of 25 stories, it improved persistent-state accuracy by 26.3 points over its base generator.
The full system streams faster than real time, at 34.3 frames per second on one 8xB200 node with the generator in BF16.
What would you like to dig into?
